coaching.title: Easy Travel Shakeout
coaching.message: No session on your calendar today and you're landing off a red-eye through Atlanta into LA — so keep it a recovery Monday. Peak Phase means the hard vert lives on your weekends; Mondays exist to flush them. Once you're on the ground, get 30-40 min fully in Zone 1 (under ~135 bpm, nose-breathing easy) or skip the run entirely and just walk 40 min. Legs first, ego never. 52 days to Kranjska Gora.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Travel day = hydration and repair, not carb-loading. Cabin air is dehydrating, so front-load water plus electrolytes on landing. Aim near your ~220g rest-day carb target spread across real meals, prioritize 100-130g protein for tissue repair after the weekend load, and lean on anti-inflammatory foods (berries, leafy greens, salmon, olive oil) to counter travel inflammation. Go easy on alcohol at the board dinner tonight.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: You've crossed time zones on no real sleep — recovery IS today's workout. Get 10-15 min of gentle mobility to un-stiffen from the flight (hips, ankles, T-spine), elevate the legs for 10 min, and protect tonight's sleep window hard: dim screens after the dinner, cool room, target 8+ hours to reset your clock toward Pacific time.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: The Julian Alps won't care how busy your July was — they'll reward the athlete who trained the boring days well. A red-eye plus a board dinner is exactly the kind of week that derails amateurs and builds pros. You're not skipping training today; you're choosing the recovery that lets Saturday's vert session actually land. Respect the small choices and the peak block takes care of itself.
